meta_desc: Class 12 Term 2 three-dimensional geometry test paper on lines, planes, skew distance and coplanarity, with a free 8-question quiz and full solutions.

quiz.title: Class 12 Three-Dimensional Geometry Quiz (Term 2)
quiz.intro: Eight Term 2 questions on direction cosines, equations of lines and planes, angles, shortest distance between skew lines and coplanarity. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: The direction ratios of a line are 2, −1, 2. Its direction cosines are:
questions.explanation: Divide each ratio by the magnitude √(2²+(−1)²+2²) = √9 = 3, giving 2/3, −1/3, 2/3.

questions.q: If a line makes angles 90°, 60° and 30° with the x, y and z axes, its direction cosines are:
questions.explanation: Direction cosines are cos of each angle: cos 90° = 0, cos 60° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2. Check: 0 + 1/4 + 3/4 = 1.

questions.q: The angle between the planes 2x − y + 2z = 5 and x + 2y + 2z = 3 is cos⁻¹ of:
The shortest distance between two intersecting lines in space is:
options: Equal to the distance between their points
questions.explanation: Intersecting lines share a common point, so the shortest distance between them is 0. A non-zero shortest distance means the lines are skew (or parallel).

questions.q: The angle φ between a line with direction vector b and a plane with normal n is given by:
questions.explanation: The angle a line makes with a plane is the complement of the angle with the normal, so sinφ = |b·n| / (|b||n|).

questions.q: The Cartesian equation of a line through (1, 2, 3) with direction ratios 3, −1, 4 is:
questions.explanation: The symmetric form is (x−x₁)/a = (y−y₁)/b = (z−z₁)/c with point (1,2,3) and ratios 3, −1, 4.

questions.q: Two lines are coplanar if the scalar triple product [ (a₂ − a₁) b₁ b₂ ] equals:
questions.explanation: Lines with position vectors a₁, a₂ and direction vectors b₁, b₂ are coplanar when the shortest distance is zero, i.e. the scalar triple product (a₂−a₁)·(b₁×b₂) = 0.

questions.q: The perpendicular distance from the point (2, 3, −1) to the plane 2x − 2y + z + 3 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Distance = |2(2) − 2(3) + (−1) + 3| / √(4+4+1) = |4 − 6 − 1 + 3| / 3 = 0/3 = 0. The point lies on the plane.

faq.q: What topics from three-dimensional geometry are important for Class 12 Term 2?
faq.a: Direction cosines and ratios, the vector and Cartesian equations of a line and a plane, the angle between two lines, a line and a plane, and two planes, the shortest distance between skew lines, and the condition for coplanarity. These carry the bulk of the marks.

faq.q: How do I find the shortest distance between two skew lines?
faq.a: Use the formula d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|, where a₁, a₂ are points on the lines and b₁, b₂ are their direction vectors. If the numerator is zero the lines are coplanar (intersecting or parallel).

faq.q: What is the difference between the angle a line makes with a plane and with the plane's normal?
faq.a: They are complementary. If the angle with the normal is θ, the angle with the plane itself is 90° − θ. That is why the line-plane angle uses sine of the dot product ratio while the line-normal angle uses cosine.

faq.q: How do I check whether two lines are coplanar?
faq.a: Compute the scalar triple product (a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂). If it equals zero the lines lie in one plane; otherwise they are skew. This is the same numerator that appears in the shortest-distance formula.
